ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Under suitable conditions such as illumination, a certain plant cultured in an environment with a CO2 concentration of 1% is rapidly transferred to an environment with a CO2 concentration of 0.003%. The changing trends of the micromolar concentrations of C3 and C5 compounds in the dark reaction of its leaves are shown in the figure. Answer the question: When the CO2 concentration is 0.003%, is the light intensity required for this plant's photosynthetic rate to be maximum higher or lower than when the CO2 concentration is 1%?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Under suitable conditions such as illumination, a certain plant cultured in an environment with a CO2 concentration of 1% is rapidly transferred to an environment with a CO2 concentration of 0.003%. The changing trends of the micromolar concentrations of C3 and C5 compounds in the dark reaction of its leaves are shown in the figure. Answer the question: When the CO2 concentration is 0.003%, is the light intensity required for this plant's photosynthetic rate to be maximum higher or lower than when the CO2 concentration is 1%?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis is time/s, and the vertical axis is relative concentration; there is a dashed dividing line at about 200 s, with the left side labeled 1% CO2 and the right side labeled 0.003% CO2. On the left side of the dashed line, curve A is at a relatively high and basically stable level, and curve B is at a relatively low and basically stable level; after transfer to 0.003% CO2, the originally higher curve A generally decreases, and the originally lower curve B clearly increases. Then reason: After the CO2 concentration suddenly decreases, CO2 fixation in the dark reaction is restricted, C3 production decreases, C5 consumption decreases and relatively accumulates, indicating that low CO2 becomes the main factor limiting photosynthesis. When the CO2 concentration is relatively low, even if illumination continues to be strengthened, the photosynthetic rate will reach the maximum value limited by CO2 earlier, so the light saturation point decreases. Therefore, under 0.003% CO2 conditions, the light intensity required for this plant's photosynthetic rate to reach the maximum is lower than under 1% CO2 conditions.
